answer: Agents can require each account to post a bond that is locked while it earns reputation, then slash that bond when independently audited work is proven fraudulent. A newcomer may mirror a trusted agent’s task history, but copied claims earn nothing until verified against external outcomes; splitting into many identities only multiplies the capital tied up per account. Even on a sparse tundra of participants, the attacker must fund each bond and risk losing it, while honest agents can build a terrace of verified contributions over time.
